Vṛishabha,
Margasirsha,
śu. di. 12 (called
gōdvadasi.)
cells.remarks: Registers that in the presence of god Vighnēśvara on the banks of the Tunga- bhadra river the king made a gift of the village Kanuma in Muṇḍumuḍugu-sīmā, a district of the Guṭṭi-vāfṭa to a number of Brahmans who were required to perform the services of a certain service at the Mahadēva- chdrēshwarship to the god Channakēshava- déva at Mundumudugu on the bank of the river Pinakini (i.e. Pennor). The grant was made at the request of a certain Appalarāja, son of Krishnarāja and grand- son of Timmarāja of the Solar race. Partly published by Dr. Fleet in Ind. Ant., Vol. VI, PP. 85 ff.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Registers the sale by a temple priest of his right of worship on four and half days in the month to raise up a portion of money which he was unable to pay towards his unmet apparel and other personal ornaments, bronze utensils, etc., belonging to the temple. The en.bezzlement, it is stated, was detected in the 28th year of the king . Reference is also made to similar misappropriations by the same person, detected in the 3rd year of Adhirajēndra-deva and in the 3rd and 11th years of Kulōttunga-Chōla-dēva, when the temple property was recovered by Rajarāja-Mūvēndavēlar, Senāpati Pallavarāyar and Sēnāpati Nardiyarāyar re-respectively. The amounts which he had thus to make good were also included in the present sale.

cells.date: 5th [date-calculation appendix, No. 117: 6th year, . . . . 10, Thursday, “Punarvasu.” The only date in the years A.D. 1258, 1259 (which would cover the 6th year of Jaṭāvarman Vīra-Pāṇḍya whether we reckon his reign from 1253 or 1254) is A.D. 1259, Thursday, November 6 (= Vṛischika 10), on which day bahula 4 ended at ·1 and Nakshatra “Punarvasu” at ·53. There is also a date in the reign of Jaṭāvarman Vīra-Pāṇḍya, who began to reign in A.D. 1296; namely A.D. 1301, Thursday, July 6 (= Karkaṭaka 10), on which date Nak. “Punarvasu” ended at ·31. In A.D. 1286, Thursday, November 7, on which day bahula 4 ended at ·19, and Nakshatra “Punarvasu” at ·61 was 11 Vṛischika not 10 Vṛischika. From this we may infer that the king referred to in this inscription was either Jaṭāvarman Vīra-Pāṇḍya whose reign began in A.D. 1253 or 1254, or the one who began to reign in A.D. 1296, not Māṛavarman Vīra-Pāṇḍya whose reign began either in A.D. 1253 or in A.D. 1280.]

cells.place: On a slab set up in the verandah of the Uddibasavaṇa temple at Morigeri (Hadagalli taluk, Bellary district).
cells.date: Śaka 967, [Pārthiva], Kārtika, Paurṇami, lunar eclipse. [date-calculation appendix, No. 441: Śaka 967, [Pārthiva], Kārttika, Puṇṇami (full-moon), lunar eclipse = A.D. 1045-46 = Pārthiva. On Monday, October 28. A.D. 1045 there was a lunar eclipse at ·60 of day.]
cells.remarks: A subordinate of the king was Trailōkyamalla Nanni-Noḷamba Pallava-Pormāḍigaḷ, who was ruling the district of Baḷḷakuṇḍe 300, Kōgaḷi 500, Kaḍamba-lige 1000, Kuḍiya-Haravi 30; and Kāviḍi 30; the five villages and the Noḷambavāḍi 32,000 province. A subordinate of the king, one Bamma-rāja, the chief of whom was Daṇḍanāyaka Tikayya were enjoying supreme authority over six villages of which Mōrigere was one. Tikayya gave some land to Sōmēśvara-Paṇḍita, pupil of Jñānēśvara-Paṇḍita, pupil of Maleyala-Paṇḍita who was the chief of Kōgaḷi 500. The record adds that Daṇḍanāyaka Tikayya built a tank and a garden to the temple of Noḷambēśvara after washing the feet of Sōmēśvara-Paṇḍita.

cells.remarks: Gives a genealogical list of the subordinate Noḷamba chiefs of Pallava descent. Trailōkyamalla Nanni-Noḷamba-Pallava-Pormāḍigaḷ (see No. 441) had a younger brother of Jagadēkamalla-Noḷamba [alias] Irmmaḍi Noḷamba, who was the son of Jagadēkamalla-Noḷamba [alias] Udayāditya, who, was the son of Iriva-beḍaṅga Noḷamba-Ghaṭeyankakāra. Registers that Tikayya and other servants established a feed-ing-house in the temple of Noḷambēśvara at Mōrigere in order to serve the parikshāsinas of Udayādityadēva and with the permission of the king, who, having returned from a raid on Sīvapa(?), was camping on his way at Paviṇapaḍaṅgili (i.e., Huvina-haḍagalli), granted the village Savandiya-pāḷa for their upkeep. The same teachers as in the previous inscription, i.e., the followers of Lakulīśa and members of Simha-parshe. The chiefs Chaṭṭarasa, Ghaṭṭiyarasa, a subordinate of Samanta-Garūḍa and others also made gifts.

cells.place: On the slab built into the wall of the Koṭṭūru temple at Koṭṭūru (same taluk and district).
cells.date:
11th Vibhava, Pushya, śu. di. 13, Friday, Uttarāyaṇa-Saṅkrānti, Vyatīpāta. [date-calculation appendix, No. 445: Śaka 1447, Kollam 701, Māsi, 7 tēdi, ba. di. chaturdaśī, Śūla-yōga, Thursday,
Hasta.
In A.D. 1526, on Thursday, February 1 [= Māsi 6 (not 7)] ba. chaturthī (not chaturdaśī) ended at ·39 and “Hasta” ended at ·35.
Māsi 7 and chaturdaśī seem to be errors for Māsi 6 and chaturthī respectively.
[The solar day and the tithi are correctly quoted.—Ep.]]
cells.remarks: Supplies a genealogical list of the Chālukya kings from Taila II. Jagadēkamalla Vīra-Pāṇḍya was the feudatory of Perma-[Jagadēkamalla II]. His maternal uncle was Vikramāditya, the son of Billa-marasa. This chief granted the village Koṭṭūru to the temple of Kōṭēśvara on the bank of the Tuṅgabhadrā river. Another gift to the same temple made in the 6th year, Rudhirōdgārin is also recorded. In the year Vilambi the Jahā-maṇḍalēśvara Vijaya-Pāṇḍya made a grant to the same temple for the merit of his maternal uncle Vikramāditya.

The 500, Nāgavarmayya-Nāyaka, the headman of Sōgi and his brothers Kājamayya-Nāyaka and Mahādēva-Nāyaka being together, made a gift of land, etc., for daily worship to be maintained in the temple of Kēśavadēva built by Nāga-varmayya-Nāyaka. Vīra-Ghaṭṭiyanna was made the guardian of the gift.

The 500, Nāgavarmayya-Nāyaka, the headman of Sōgi and his brothers Kājamayya-Nāyaka and Mahādēva-Nāyaka being together, made a gift of land, etc., for daily worship to be maintained in the temple of Kēśavadēva built by Nāga-varmayya-Nāyaka. Vīra-Ghaṭṭiyanna was made the guardian of the gift.Read more (1 KB)

cells.place: On the pedestal of the Sarasvati image in the Bhimesvara-Deva temple at Hire-Hadagali (same taluk and district).
cells.remarks: Damaged. The King, as a crown prince, was ruling the provinces Gangavadi 96,000, Banavase 12,000 and Nolambavadi 32,000, from the minister Dama- rasa is stated to have commenced the rule of Damesvara at Post-Vadagale which was a village of Brahmans from the time of Janamejaya. About the end of the inscription is made of the Hoysala King Vishnu or Vira-Vishnu Tribhuva-namalla.

cells.date: Hāmalādhi, Vaiśākha, (Purnnami) full-moon Sunday, lunar eclipse and Chalukya-Vikrama-varsha 32, Sarvajit, Chaitra Amā-vāsya, (new-moon), Monday, solar eclipse and Vishnu-Samk-ramana. [date-calculation appendix, No. 495: Saka 1183, Prajapati, Magha ; śukla tritiya, Sunday. In A.D. 1271–72 (= Ś. 1133 = Prajapati), Māgha śu. 3 ended on Tuesday, 5 January, A.D. 1272 at ·26 of day. Su. 1 of the same month ended at ·43 on Sunday, 3 January and śu. 2 at ·35 on Monday 4 January. Su. 3 in the inscription is probably an error for śu. 2 which began on Sunday at ·43.]
cells.remarks: Damaged. The record begins with a genealogical list of the Hoysalas down to Vishnu with Perma-Jagadekamalla II. It states that the Mahā-maṇḍaleśvara Vira-Pandyadeva was ruling Kadambalige 1,000, Ballakunde 300 and Kogali 500. It is made Vira-Pandya made a grant of land for the temple of Mallikarjuna-deva and his daughter Mahadeviyarasu.

cells.remarks: The charter is very late for the Saka year quoted but agree very well with the time of Tribhuvana-malla Vikramaditya VI. cells.place: On a slab in a field to the north of the same village.
cells.date: Śaka 1481, Siddhārthin, Jyēshṭha, ba. di. 7. [date-calculation appendix, No. 510: Do. do.]
cells.remarks: Gift of timber required for baling water to the charity-fountain at Chhatradahalli, by certain residents of the village which belonged to the temple of Malyavanta Raghunāthadēva. On the same day certain salt manufacturers (uppāra) the same village were granted the right to give the half-as of salt from each salt-pan to the one who baled out water for the fountain; the smiths too who were worshippers of Kālikādēvi and Kāmathē-śvara agreed to repair or renew the iron bucket for drawing water and the gauṇḍas gave a piece of land for the maintenance of the man.

cells.date: Śaka 1468, Krōdhin, Māgha, śu. di. 15. [date-calculation appendix, No. 514: Saka 990, Kilaka, Margasira, Full-moon, Friday, lunar eclipse. In A.D. 1068, Friday, Aug. 15; su. 15 ended at °15 of day, and there was a lunar eclipse on this day. The month was Bhadrapada and not Margasira. In this year, Margasira su. 15 fell on Wednesday. Margasira in the inscription is probably an error for Bhadrapada.]
cells.remarks: Records the foundation of a new village called Chiku Timmaṇapura-agrahāra, for the merit of Tirumalamma, the daughter of Aliya-Rāmarāja. She is stated to have been a madavalige kumāri i.e., a daughter about to be married. The record is dated in the year 1468 within the Vijayanagara, Śrāvaṇa, is one of Rāmāyaṇatya who is described as a feudatory of Achyuta.

cells.remarks: Registers that the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Ghaṭṭarasa, son of the Āhavamalla Chāvuṇḍarasa, caused a gift of land to be made by Eṛaka-gauṇḍa of Koḷaguṇḍe, to the temple of Bāḷēśvara built by his father, Ghaṭṭarasa (who is described as a great chief). His chief dāyāda who succeeded to the place of his father after the latter's death is stated to have been enjoying Mānavāḍi 140, Poḷalagaṇḍe, the village of Koḷaguṇḍe and the landed property (jīvita) of the palace servants (aramaṇe-mūla [?]).

cells.place: In the same place; left of entrance
cells.date: Śaka 1452, Vikṛiti, Chaitra, ba. di. 30, Monday.
cells.remarks: Chandraśēkharamātya, ruling the Śisula-rājya as the king's representative (avasaram), built maṇṭapa in the inner court of the Mallikārjuna temple, presented golden images of Nandīśvara and Bhṛiṅgīśvara, set up standing stone figures of his master Kṛishṇarāya, his father-in-law Dēmaśē and of himself in that maṇṭapa and for meeting the expenses of worshipping the god in that maṇṭapa, the village of Koṭagotta which the king had given him was included within his jurisdiction. He also gave a golden cup and a silver pedestal (pānavaṭṭam) for the god, set up to the north of Mallikārjuna the liṅga called Dēmayya and set up in front of it a golden pillar. At Nāgalāpuram he erected at the foot of the hill a temple for Viṭhala (i.e. Vīrabhadra), connected a liṅga called Dēmayya within it and presented the village Dēnasamudra to Brahmans.

cells.place: On the west face of the right pillar in the same place.
cells.date: Śaka 1438, Yuva, Śrāvaṇa, śu. di. 15, Wednesday, = 11th July 1516, lunar eclipse.
cells.remarks: Records that the Redḍis and Mullaras in the service of the king Krishṇadēvarāya worshipped the god. Registers the conquests of Krishṇadēvarāya and states that after making gifts at Amarāvatī he came to Śrīśailam and had maṇḍapas constructed in the car street. Prior to this in the year Śaka 1438 (Yuva), in the day of the lunar eclipse, he made a gift of the villages of Pommanahāḷḷa and Aṭukūru to the temple of Mallikārjuna. He also remitted tolls on hēvadis, pack horses, bullocks, asses and head-loads.

cells.date: Śaka 1438, Yuva, Pushya, śu. di. 15, Friday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 64: 31st year, Kanyā, śu. di. 3, Friday, “Svāti.” In my article in the Ind. Ant. (June to August 1913) I placed the accession of Māṛavarman Vīra-Pāṇḍya in A.D. 1253, a year earlier than that of Jaṭāvarman Vīra-Pāṇḍya of Iḷam and Koṅgu fame. In one recent case the Epigraphist thought the characters of this reign were later than those of Jaṭāvarman Vīra-Pāṇḍya of 1254 and I am, therefore, tentatively suggesting dates 27 years later than those previously arrived at for Māṛavarman Vīra-Pāṇḍya. In the present case I suggest, as a tentative equivalent A.D. 1310, September 25 (= Kanyā 28); śu. 3 commenced at ·67, ending next day at ·66; while “Svāti” ended on Friday at ·61.]
cells.remarks: Refers to the conquests of Krishṇarāya in the east and states that on his second campaign against Kalinga he visited Ahōbala and presented to the god a necklace, a pendant set with diamonds and an emerald, 5 gold-gilt umbrellas, a golden plate and 1000 varāhas. His queen also made a gift of land to the god. The village Maduru in Changaḷa-māri-sīma was also granted for providing offerings to the god.

cells.remarks: Registers that Rāmānuja-jīyangāru, the agent (madarakā) of Vān-Saṭhagōpa-jīyangāru, the manager of the Ahōbalam temple, and Mahārāja Rāmarāja Tirumalarāja-dēva-Mahārāja sold 5 marakkāls of land to Obulrāju and grandson of the Mahōmaṇḍalēśvara Pōṇḍirāju-Rāmarājayyangāru of the Solar race and the Viśvāmitra-gōtra. This chief gave it back to the temple on the condition that 30 bags of paddy realized from the land each year was to be utilized for daily offerings in the shrine of Nammālvār situated in the Bhārgava street near the shrine of Prahlāda-Varada in the Ahōbalamvara Kṣētra-Tirupati and that the offerings were to be distributed among the Jīyangārus.

In A.D. 1454 (= Bhāva), Vaisākha, śu. 15 fell on Friday (not Thursday), April 12, and ended at ‘94.]
cells.remarks: Gives a long account of how Veṅkaṭādridēva-Choḷamahārāja, a prince of the Solar race and t. s. Kāśyapa-gōtra, came to receive certain privileges in the temple. Under orders of the king and at the request of Vān-Saṭhagōpa-jīyangāru, his grand father, Koṇḍarāju-Kondarāju-Tirumalarāja had expelled the Muḥammadān chief Vibhurāma who had occupied the temple of Ahōbalam for seven years in alliance with the ṭhaṇḍavāru (chiefs). It was for thus restoring the temple to its original family that the family was granted the privileges mentioned above.

21st Mēsha, śu. di. 13, Sunday, [Hasta].
Sunday 13th April, A.D. 1253, which was śu. 13 and a day of "Hasta", is probably meant: the tithi ended at ·58 and the nakshatra ended at ·27 of Sunday. It was the 20th year of the king's reign. The solar date was, however, 20th Mēsha, not 21st as stated in the inscription.]
cells.remarks: Gift of 90 sheep for a lamp by the assembly of the adinart-galam, including the young and the old, met to-gether in the big hall called Senbiyamahadevi-perumandapam built by the king, and agreed to pay the taxes on certain temple lands from the interest on the specified gold which they said they had received from the temple treasury. Kuddur is called the northern hamlet of the village. One of the signatories was the accountant.

cells.place: On the broken Garuḍa-pillar of the same temple.
cells.king: Bhīma, husband of Sōmāmbā or Sōmadēvi.
cells.remarks: Beginning 1st and much damaged. Registers the genealogy of a Brahman family of ministers who served under the Koṭa kings of Dhānyakaṭaka. Vallabha, the minister of Koṭa-Bhīma established at Rompicheru (Paṅkaṭāṭapura, the temple of Ananta-Gōpinātha in the name and for the merit of his deceased father Ananta. Gifts of lands, wells and tolls are also recorded. The first few lines state that the pillar was made for the Gōpinātha of Mallaya-Nāyaku, son of Jāyapa-Nāyadu. Registers a gift of land made by a certain Vallabha-Fregga, in favour of Lakshmaṇadāsa, the manager (śrīkaraṇa) of the temple of Ananṭu-Gōpinātha. Also refers to gifts of money and of grants for the maintenance of lamps in the same temple. Mentions a certain Rāmānujadāsa, a disciple of the Vaisnava teacher Nallāṇḍichakravarti. This compound wall was the gift of Channaya, a servant of Voḍgala-Nāyadu.

cells.place: On the Naga-pillar set up in front of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Registers that Māra, son of Iśvara-Nāyaka the here-ditary minister of the king, constructed two big tanks, built a temple for Sōmēśvara and a pond at Koppara-grāma. The king visited the god Sōmēśvara and granted to him the village Koppara-grāma; so also prince Choḍa-Balli, the younger brother of the king, gave to the temple Koppara. The grants were confirmed by the Mahāmaṇḍaleśvara Kadiyarāja, a subordinate of Vishṇuvardhana, at the request of Māra. The Kāḷamukha ascetic Mallikarjuna of Pāluru was placed in charge of the Sōmēśvara temple. On another face of the same pillar are recorded gifts of lamps evidently to the same temple and of sheep required to maintain these lamps.

cells.place: On a stone near the Āñjanēya temple
cells.remarks: Broken at the bottom. Registers that the temple of Kōmaṭi-Kōṭēśvara-svāmin at Koḷalapuḍi in Koṇḍavīḍu-sīma were consecrated for the merit of Paṇḍrāju, Vallabhārāju and others whose ancestors claim a long list of historically interesting birudas. They were of the Durjava race, lords of Koḷḷikāpura and rulers of the Shaṭsahasra country on the south side of the river Krishṇavēṇī (i.e. Kṛishṇā). See Epigraphia Indica, Volume VI, page 224.

cells.place: On the Nāga-pillar set up in front of the Vīrabhadra temple in the same village.
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Refers to a line of kings or chiefs commencing with Bhīma, who were the lords of Koḷḷipāka, the Shaṭsahasra country on the southern side of Krishna, etc. In this family was a certain Guṇḍa who made gifts of land to Bhīma-dēvara of Koḷḷipāka. Below this is a later record which registers the lands enjoyed by certain head-karṇams. Mentions the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Parichchēdi-Bhīma.

cells.location: Tuḷḷūru
cells.place: On the Naga-slab set up near a Vinayaka shrine
cells.remarks: Begins with the eulogy of a certain Kāpa of the fourth caste. Mentions Buddhavarman of the Gonka-family, and his son, Sītapāda-Nāyaka. The grandsons of the latter served under Maṇḍa and gained a victory at Manuēru on behalf of their overlord, and received from him the villages Tuṃbūru and Aṭukūru. Next came Kāpana who served under Chōḍa (son of) Veḷanāṇḍi Gōṅka and set up the temple of Mahādēva at Tuḷḷūru and gave a lamp, etc., and the village of Bēḍavāra, the gift which included shares for the several services, the writer of the record, Brāhmaṇas, etc.

cells.place: On a second slab ying in the same place
cells.date: Chālukya Vikrama year 31, ‘Jyaya, śuddha-full-moon, Full-moon (Puṇṇami), Wednesday, lunar eclipse.
cells.remarks: The missing top portion of the stone was discovered at Maṭakkapuram 7 miles from Pedda-Tumbalam. Records that the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Kāva-Ṇallarasa granted the taxes of Baḍagikuṇṭe in Tumbala thirty, a sub-division of Ādavani five hundred, in Sindavāḍi-nāḍu, to the temple of Kaṇṭakṇadēva for worship, offerings, repairs, etc.; he also presented some land and a village. The great nagaras of the great city Tumbala, the baṇañjigas, the nānādēśis, the nobles and the mahājanas are mentioned.

cells.remarks: The king's brother Tuḷuvakōmalla-Noḷamba-Pallava-Perumāḍi Jayasinghadeva was ruling the Noḷambavāḍi 32,000 and the Sindavāḍi-one-thousand, from his capital town of Kampile. cells.place: On a slab set up near the eastern wall of the Kaṇuma-Doḍḍayya's temple near Kotakalu.
cells.remarks: Evidently the slab belongs to the village of Pedda Kaṇṭalūru. Records a genealogical account of the chiefs Brama (Brammidēva), his son Paḍmidēva and Vatsarāja the maternal uncle of the latter. Paḍmidēva and Vatsarāja were ruling the whole of the eastern country including Sindavāḍi. The village Kaṇṭalūru in Rāgi 12, a sub-division of Sindavāḍi-one-thousand, was granted to the temple of Brahmēśvara (at Kaṇṭalūru) and the Kiriṇāryāpura, the capital of the Sindavāḍi province) which had been built by the merchant Śrōtriya Eyyama-seṭṭi.

cells.place: On a slab set up near the Rājarājēśvarasvāmin temple at Cheruvu-Belagallu (Kurnool taluk and district).
cells.remarks: Damaged. Registers that the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Kāmārāja-rājayyādēva-Mahārāja remitted the taxes on Cheruvu-Belagallu, Bāgēpalli, etc., which was part of the Adavāni-sīma. Registers that the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Siddhanuju Sītarāmarājyadēva-Mahārāja, having conferred the tolls of Kere-Belagallu-hāṇyam on the chief Chennamanu, the latter granted 6 tardhas, collected from the Bājar of that city, for offerings, to the temple of Rājarājēśvara-Mahādēva at Kere-Belagallu-pilla. Other gifts made in the following year Dummati, are also recorded.

cells.place: On a pillar set up in front of the Vira-bhadrasvāmin temple in the same village.
cells.remarks: Gift of land by Sunkana-Nuyaka, son of Dādi-Nayaka to the temple of Vīra-bhadradēva of Kere-Belaguli (included in Adavani-durga) which was granted as dēvadāna free of tax extending..... in charters of about the 12th century A.D. cells.place: On the Jaina image of Vardhamānasvāmin (now worshipped as a Hindu idol) at Kammarachodu (Alur taluk, Bellary district).
cells.remarks: Damaged. Mentions first the Mahāmandulēsvara Vallabha-Chōla-Mahārāja who was ruling the Sira-vāda-thousand province and whose prasasti begins with the words Charanā-saraṇaha, etc.; then it mentions the Mahāmandalēsvara Chōkarasa of the Mahabali race whose prasasti begins with the words Jayatgētā, etc., and next the Mahā-sāmantas Chandarasa, Barramarasa and Rāvarasa of Kondakunde, whose prasasti begins with the words ari-durdhara, etc., seems to record the grant of a land.

cells.remarks: Records that as there was no money in the treasury of the temple of Piṇakkaruṭaiya-Nayanār in Pirānka-chaturvēdimangalam a brāhmaṇa of Piṇākka-chaturvēdimangalam a brāhmaṇa in Ari-nādu, a certain Puliyūr-kilavan Pirālaya- Viḍangan Abhayampakkan living in the street called Kulaśēkharapperuṇderu, defrayed the expenses to be met in regard to the tax called viniyōgam on the bank Ulaguyyavanda-Pāṇḍyapērarēri and made a gift of one-third of the dry land yielding income from the tank along with some money to the temple, for offerings to Tiruppuliyarai- Nāchchiyār and Tukhaiyār. Mentions the temple of Tirukkaṅkalvaramud-iya-Nāyanār at Savadam- paṭṭakurichi which belonged to the tantiravārar i.e. The Kalkoḷas the Sēnāpat is and Doṇdanāyakan.

cells.remarks: Gift of land to a number of persons of various gōtras and sūtras. cells.place: On the south wall of the rock-cut temple of Mahadeva at Mahiyadarkurichi (same taluk and district)
cells.remarks: The introduction commences with the words svasti sri. Registers a gift of land by the king to the temple of Pipikagukku-Mahadeva at Mahiyadarkurichi, the southern half of Puram- pun-nadu, a subdivision of Ari-nādu. In Ari-nādu. When ordering the grant, the king was in his palace at Tirumuvõli in Kīvamba-nādu. Mentions Virapāndiyan Pilāru and the neat called Mayilādaraiyan. Below this is an incomplete record dated in the 11th year, probably of the same king.

cells.date: Lost [date-calculation appendix, No. 611: Maravarman alias Sundara-Pandya. * + 1st year, Vrischika, 2[5], ba. 1, Sunday, “ Rohini.” The regnal year as well as the day of solar month being uncertain, it is not possible to say which of the three Maravarman Sundara-Pandyas who reigned in the 13th century is referred to in the inscription. cells.remarks: Registers a dēvadāna grant of the village of Kiḷama-nallūr together with Embaḷkuppam in Teṟ-Kōṇāḍu, for offerings, to the temple of Tirukkuḍokuḷḍi-Kuḍa-Nāyanar in Poṇṇamāḷai-nādu on the occasion of the Ūshā pūjā. The gift was made for the merit of Tippasa-daṇḍāniyar, by his agent Mallaya-Nāyakar. The inscription states that Narasimha-Nayaka was governing the country on behalf of Naraśiṅga Bhūpālarāya Daṇḍanāyaka.

cells.remarks: States that the lands comprised in the village of Mapuṇūr alias Sundarapāṇḍiyan-chaturvēdimangalam, founded in the king's name by his son Kandiyadēvan, excepting those belonging to the temple of Tiruk- koḍuṅguṟuṇḍaiya-Nāyaṇār, were divided into 24 parts, 20 of which were assigned to 20 Brāhmaṇas learned in the vēdas and śāstras, 2 to the temple of Sundarapāṇḍiya-Īśvaramudaiya- Nāyaṇār and 2 to the temple of Kulaśēkhara- Viṇṇagar-Ālvār. cells.king: Māravarman alias Tribhuvanachakravartin Sundara-Pāṇḍyadēva, 'who was pleased to take the Chōla country.'
cells.remarks: Records that, at the instance of the king's nephew Kulasekharadēva, certain lands situated in Kumāṟ-rukkūṛu-kūṟram, an arid tract (palai-nilam), tax-free and given to the temple of Tirukkōlakkuḍi for offerings to the goddess of Aludaiya-Nāchchiyar Tirukkōmakkōṭṭam set up in the temple, by a native of Rajavallipuram in Kilveṁba-nāḍu. Mentions the royal seat called Palliggidam Malava-rāyan placed in the Rājas[a]lujaṅg-maṇḍapa of the king's palace at Madura(urai)pâti Kalai-kāṇi-uḍaiyārg[u]lai-vaṉadu, a district of Sōla-maṇḍalam and the temples Tandoṇdrīśvaramudaiyār and Kaṇṇi[n]āṭṭu-Viggauarajāyar.

cells.remarks: Records the sale of the kaiyāmaimai right of certain temple lands, to a native of Tirupputtūr. The pur- chaser was a resident of Kīḻ-kuṉṟūr-nāṭṭu-talaivayil, a village in the same district or Sōḻa-maṇḍalam. It was stipulated that the purchaser should bring into cultivation the waste lands. Refers to a tank called Pāṇava[n]gāndari dug in the name of the king's son (mukkāḍayār) K[a]rakrama-Pāṇḍya- Mahābāli-Vāṇadhāriyan.

cells.place: On the west wall of the same maṇḍapa
cells.date:
Śaka 1364 (Dundubhi), Purattāsi. [date-calculation appendix, No. 136: Ś. 1199, Pushya, śu. 5, Monday, Makara-Sankrānti.
In Śaka 1199 proper = A.D. 1277–78 the month Pausha was kshaya or suppressed,
and Makara-Sankrānti in that year fell on Sunday 26, December 1277 A.D.
which was Margasira ba. 15, corresponding to ordinary Pausha ba. 15.
But in Ś. 1199 current = A.D. 1276–77, Makara-Sankrānti fell on Friday 25th
December, A.D. 1276; the 1st Makara was Saturday 26 December on
which day Pausha bahula 5 (not śukla 5) commenced at ·47; it ended next
day at ·38. [The inscription has śudha (i.e. śukla) 5 — Ep.]]

cells.remarks: Gift of the village Cōndravūru in Guddavāḍi-viṣaya to certain Brāhmaṇas, by the chief Mahādēva of the solar race, whose minister was Mallikārjuna. The Sanskrit language in which the inscription is written is very corrupt. Seems to record the sale of the village Taṭēśvara-grāma and mentions Sīlāditya and some (chiefs of the) family of the Vāga family. The characters are of the 13th century, like those of the plates of Daṇḍimahādēvī (Epigraphia Indica, Vol. VI, p. 136).

cells.remarks: These two plates (without ring) are written on four sides in two different types of character. The bigger letters (of perhaps a later date) belong to the time of Kalyāṇakalaśa [Nōtri-bhañja] and commence like those his Ganjam plates already published with text and translation in Journal of Bengal Asiatic Society, Vol. 6, pages 667 to 671. The smaller characters are of the same type as those of the Buguda plates of Mādhavavarman and begin similarly (Epigraphia Indica, Volume VII, p. 10f). The first plate is missing.

cells.remarks: In Śālivāhana-Śaka 1280, Plavaṅga, Kārttika śu. 15, solar eclipse (?), the gaudike of the village Aṇṇadāni-gauḍa was submitted to the (village) court (dharmāsana) by Jīrūru-Boma-Sōmayājin. The latter had received it as dīkṣā-harā mahātra from the king Gaṇḍada Dēvarāya. The āyagāras for the new village were appointed in the presence of the residents of four villages. The village seems to have been surnamed Borje.

cells.remarks: In th. Epigraphia Indica. A quarrel regarding the gaudike of Bole between Aṇṇadāni-Gauḍa and Chigamudaiya was submitted to the (village) court (dharmāsana) consisting of the chief men of the twelve village tenants (āyagāras). cells.remarks: Lease of 20 mā of land in Paṇai alias Kaṭṭikāmanipuram in Muḷḷi-nāḍu, to the cultivator Agaṭṭadi Iḷaiyān Kaṭṭāṇḍi in order to maintain the service of the Vīra-Kēraḷan-sandi. The lease was sanctioned by the king in Kollam 670, Āṇi, 26 tedi, when he was camped at the fort. This result in the provision of the needs of the temple for which this maintenance was made appears as Kaṇḍan Śāttan of Saṭṭarpaṭṭi in Kaḷḷadaikkurichi.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Order to the assembly of Rājarāja-chaturvēdimaṅgalam stating that the hamlet newly founded to the south of that village the right of kaḍamai was to be held by the temple of Tirunelvēli and the right of kāṟāṇmai by a certain Ivaichōḻa-Perumāḷ Iḷaiyaṉ alias Kaḷiṅgarāyar. The hamlet was thus to be entered in accounts as a rent-free dēvadāna. The document was signed by Poṟṟēṉ-uḍaiyāṉ Kulāśēkhara-Vaḷadāraṉ and others. The word 'oḍu' at the end indicates that the record may have been a copy.

cells.date: 20th year, Dhanus, 7 tēdi, ba. di. saptami, Monday, Uttara- Phālguṇi (Uttiram).
cells.remarks: Sale of garden land belonging to two childless widows of Rajarāja-chaturvēdimangalam for 12½ śaṇai-achchu to the shrine of Kulashēkhara-Perumāḷ by their representatives (muḍukkuṟam), one a son-in-law and the other the father. The widows had previously approached the temple authorities for their iṟai for help; but failing to do this, other villagers permitted the widows to dispose of the lands as they liked.

cells.place: On the north base of the same temple
cells.remarks: The king being seated on his throne called Muḍigoṇḍachōḻan in his palace at Sabhāpati alias Sarvalōkāśrayapuram in Kil-Sembi-nāḍu, ordered the grant 1 vēli of land at Kuḍarai-ōṭṭi after making the necessary entries in the revenue registers (ulvari). The land was also exempted from antarāyam as per verbal order passed in the 4th year and the 92nd day, by the king when he was seated on the throne at Muḍigoṇḍachōḻan in his palace at Madura east of Maḍakkulam. The entries in the ulvari register regarding the antarāyam exemption are next entered. The triple form of the document is thus interesting.

cells.location: Śiriyambapuram
cells.place: On the south wall of the prakara of the Arikēsavanallūr temple
cells.date: Kōṭṭanai- 8924 (Records 9th year is given in the body of the inscription).
cells.remarks: Gift of the village Śōkkiḷakuḷam the eastern hamlet of Rājarāja-chaturvēdimangalam for maintaining lamps in the temple of Arikēsava-nāya-Nāyaṇār at Arikēsavanallūr in Muḷi-nāḍu. The gift was made at the suggestion of Kāḷingarayar, by the (king's) younger brother Tirunē-vēli Bhāgavati Aḷagapperumāḷ alias Kulashēkhara-Kandiya-dēvar who was also the donor of the lamps. The document is signed by the (king's) secretary, Tōṇḍaimān and two others. The assembly of Rājarāja-chaturvēdimangalam in the presence of Nālayiravēḷān and Rājanārāyaṇa-Mūvēndavēḷār ort the royal orders fixing the assessment at 5 achchu per year and excluded the granted lands from the vari register.

cells.location: Valudūr
cells.place: On the north wall of the Agīśvara temple
cells.king: Māṛavarman alias Tribhuvanachakra-vartin Sundara-Pāṇḍyadēva, ‘who having taken the Chola country was pleased to perform the anointment of heroes at Muḍigoṇḍaśōlapuram.’
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction பூமாது வளர்ந்த. The king being seated on his throne Malavarāyaṉ in his palace called Āyiram-uḍaiyāṉ in the temple of Madurōdaya-īśvaramuḍaiyār at the request of Valudūruḍaiyāṉ, the lands be given as tax-free dēvadāna with all income to the temple of Tiruvakīśvaramuḍaiyār at Valudiyūr, the north-eastern hamlet of Rājarāja-chaturvēdimangalam. It was also ordered by Tribhuvanachakravartin Rōṇērimāḷakoṇḍāṉ (i.e. the emperor in good health) in the 15th year and 405th day that the grant may be registered (a copy of the order furnished (அச்சீட்டு எழுதிக் கொடுத்தபடி)). The registry was also made in the same year and the record was engraved evidently on the 542nd day after the 15th year.

cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction பூமிமகள் ஜயமகள் etc. Registers that the assembly of Rājarāja-chaturvēdimangalam gave a kaniṭṭi document to the temple of Tiru-Agnīśvaramuḍaiyār at Vaḷudiyūr in obedience to the orders and the kaḍaiyīḍu of the king which they conferred on the said temple for the merit of the king as specified in the same. cells.place: On the gōpura of the same temple
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction ... Registers the gift of vēli of land at Nellukuppaikkuḍi to the shrines of Māsapāva-Aḷvār alias Nīlaṇi-Aḷavār-Perumāḷ and Nīlaṇi-Aḷavār in the temple of Tiruvīra-Vīra-Paṇḍya-Aḷvār, at Vaḍapaḷaikkalam the north-eastern hamlet of Rājarāja-chaturvēdimangalam. The king's order to make the gift was executed and the document engraved on stone. The first of the shrines was built by Paḍiyaṇi-Bhagavati alias Kaṇḍyadēva of Tirunelvēli. Ordered that the above document be duly registered and reported.

cells.place: On the west and south walls of the mandapa in front of the same shrine.
cells.king: Maravarman alias Tribhuvanachakra-vartin Sundara-Pandyadeva, who being pleased to take the Chola country was pleased to perform the anointment of heroes and victors at Mudigondachōlapuram
cells.remarks: The members of the village (ōr) who performed the Sēnāpati-tiangam and dundayanāyakam and the kārālar alias the kārālar of the village of Sirugudi in Kīl-Kallūr-nādu alias Vikrama-Pandyavalanādu their maintenance (jivita). Lands under Apārkulam to Dāsarathn-Ramēśvaramudaiyar in the temple of Śrī-Kailāsam of that village in order that the worship and offering to the several gods and goddesses set up by them in that temple may be conducted. In doing this, the temple was required to pay some money to these different mortgages and to get the lands. The donor had to pay the pattam, vijadu and varipādu on these lands by reserving for themselves 1 kalam of paddy on each ma of wet-land on which crops had been raised.

Registers that the assembly of Sēravan-mahādēvi-chaturvēdimangalam assigned a portion of a land already in the enjoyment of the temple in lieu of another which they had granted to the temple on the occasion of its foundation, the latter being disputed to have been the gift of another Vishnu temple in the same village Sēravan-mahādēvi. cells.place: On the south wall of the same mandapa.
cells.remarks: Registers the royal order issued at the request of Maḷavarāyan to grant some land at Seyyapaḍainallūr and Dēśimākkā-l-kkuḍi as tax-free devādāna to the temple of Tiruvirāmēśvaramuḍaiyār at Śivallamurudaiyār to register the same in the ulvari and to report. The income was for the purpose of providing offerings and maintaining the festival of Paṅguni-Uttaram, his birth-day asterism, instituted in that temple by Vīra-Pāṇḍyadēva-Vaḷḷavarāyar compare No. 556. The actual grant was made in the 11th year of the king.

cells.date: Kollam 577, Āvaṇi, 10 tāti, śu. di. Friday, daśami, Śravaṇa.
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Refers to the repair and reconsecration of the temple of Teṇ-Tiruvēṅgaḍa-Viṇṇagar-Emberumān at Bha-vānidī-tīrtha on the southern bank of the big river Tām-raparṇam (i.e. Tāmraparṇī), worshipped (in early times) by the sage Rōmaśa-maharshi. The lands belonging to the temple were placed in the hands of the śrīpāda and the chief Mārtāṇḍa-Aḍigal of Jayasiṅgha-nāḍu, for being managed and used for the temple and the matha. The liere also to three women-servants to do service in the temple and in the matha.

Registers that Mukundanātha-Śripāda, a teacher in the line of Parāśarabhaṭṭar Paivajakāchārya Dēvēndrapuri, appointed one of his capable pupils to manage the business connected with the temple of Ten-Tiruveṅgaḍanāyar and his own maṭha. cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Records the reconstruction of the temple of Uḍaiyavar at Śevval alias Kaṇaviniya-Pāṇḍya-chaturvēdimangalam, on its being deserted during the occupation of the Muhammadans for some time, by Muṭṭachōhai Kaṇḍan Karaḷan of Muḍiyūr-Illar in Kurukkēṇi-Kollam. He is stated to have renamed the village as Vīrakēralanallūr, to have started the repairs in the year 669 and to have renovated the whole temple from upāna to stupi, to have founded a shrine for the goddess summoning with the harshana ceremony and to have built the other portions such as the maha-maṇḍapa, sōpāṇa etc. He also appointed temple accountants, servants etc., with certain privileges and provided for the daily worship and festivities in the temple, by grants of lands.

cells.remarks: Stone damaged at the end. Seems to record the remission of taxes with effect from the 10th year of reign, on some lands at Kallūr in Mēḷ-Vemba-nāḍu in Muḍigoṇḍachōḷa-vaḷanāḍu, in favour of the temple of Kailāsamuḍaiyār-Mahādēva, by the king when he was seated in the [western] hall of his palace at Rājēndrēśōḷapuram, at the instance of his maternal uncle (ammāṇ). Mentions the items of money-income (āyam) and the local officers (adhikāri) including the ūrkkaḷañju and refers to a number of officers of the king. The lands received the new name of Śivapādāśēkharanallūr.

Registers that the king while seated on his throne called Aṇṇāyadarāyaṇ in his palace at Tirunelvēli, Vēmbā-nāḍu, ordered that 1/2 (vēli) of land might be granted as tax-free dēvadāna to the temple of Śrīvallabha-Āḷvār which is situated in the “tirumālīgai”, i.e., the sacred shrine in the centre of Śēravanmahādēvi-caturvēdimangalam in Muḷi-nāḍu, for the daily offerings of the god.

cells.place: On the west tier of the same maṇḍapa
cells.remarks: The right end of the inscription is built in. Records that the images of Rāma, Sītā and Lakshmaṇa were set up in the temple of Śrīvallabha-Viṇṇagar-Emberumāṇ and were taken in procession in the 15th regnal year. It states that a grant of tax-free land was made evidently by the king as part of madhuparka-dakshiṇā, for conducting worship and offerings.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Stones misplaced in re-building. Portions of the historical introduction of the king etc. of Jātavarman Kulasekhara-dēva are found here. The king is said to have been called Muḍikonda-pāṇḍiyan in his palace at Madurai [east of Madakkulam] in Madurāḍaya-vaḷanāḍu, promised the remission of taxes on certain lands belonging to the temple, for the daily offerings of the god Ḍavi[yannāyaka]r-Muḍaiya-Mahādēva. Registers that this is the kaṭṭaḷai for a gift of land already made to the shrine of Kaṭṭaḍuṇḍēva.

cells.remarks: Records that at the suggestion of his brother-in-law Koḍai Ravi-varman (i.e., Ravivarman), the king ordered that the land in the village of Śōravam-mahādēvi-chaturvēdimangalam be made completely tax-free for daily offerings, the recital of the Vedas and Purāṇas and for singing, dancing, etc. at the service instituted in the name of the former in the temple of Tavarājatyaiyār. The order was actually issued on the 2638th day after the 3rd year.

cells.remarks: Records the order given by the king that the worship in the Govindarāja-Perumāḷ temple at Tirupati must be conducted on the same lines as that of Tiruvengaḷanātha on the Tirumala hill and that Kandala Rāmānujayya and his pupils should supervise the distribution of prasāda to the Śrī-vaishnavas, both foreign and local. It also mentions the Govindarāja-samnidhi and in the Rāmānujakūṭa (feeding house) newly constructed by him at Tirupati. The king also instituted a Rāmānujakūṭa (feeding house) on the hill and fixed the scale of worship of god Tiruvengaḷanātha to be supervised by the same Kandala Rāmānujayya. Some services in the temple were rendered by the 'hatada (P) Śrī-Vaishnavas Aḷagiya-Perumāḷ of Tiruchchanūr is also mentioned.

cells.location: Palla-banda
cells.place: On a pillar set up in the court yard of the Ranganāthasvāmin temple
cells.remarks: Registers that under orders of the Mahāmaṇḍaleśvara Rāma-rāja-Tirumala-rājayyadēva-Mahā-arasu, the Mahājanas of Ādhavya Timmaya-Nāyaka of Nidugal and the gauḍas and eṇabhōva residents of that province together with the merchants, gave Tumukuru-rājya to the temple of Tiruvengalanātha at Peyyalabande for offering, worship, and festivals. The gift was actually made on the 11th day. Mentions Keñchappa-Nāyaka the mudra-officer of Gutti-Tirumalarāja-yyadēva-Mahā-arasu evidently the same as Rāmarāja-Tirumalarājayyadēva-Mahā-arasu.

cells.place: On the second pillar of the same temple..
cells.remarks: This maṇḍapa was erected by Areyam Bajarajām alias Vikramachōḷa-Chōḷiyavaraiyan, the chief of Chattaṇan-gaḷam in Tirumūr-nāḍu and the commander of the forces (of the king), on the 40th day opposite the 160th day (of this year). Below this on a separate section of the pillar are engraved the titles Chōḷa-Chōḷiyavaraiyan and the names Sāmaṇṭabharāṇan in Kanarese and Nāṇmadi-Bhīman Sāmaṇṭabharāṇan in Tamil. These may have been the titles of the chief who built the maṇḍapa.

cells.place: On a pillar set up in the courtyard of the Jaina temple in the same village.
cells.king: Mahāmaṇḍaleśvara Tribhuvanamalla Niḍugal-kapu Āpachakravarti Vīra-nava-Murāri, Irugupadēva-Chōḷa Mahārāja of the Chōḷa race ruling at the capital town of Niḍugallu.
cells.remarks: Registers that Mallisetti son of Sōbhagavana-Bommisetti and Mēḷavve the favourite lay disciple of Bāḷadēva-Mahādhāri-dēva who was the senior pupil of Tribhuvanakīrtirāvuḷa of Ingōḷēśvara, of the Mūla-saṅgha, Dēśiya-gaṇa, Koṇḍakuṇḍa-anvaya and Pustaka-gachchha, gave at Tammadaḷḷi the 2,000 areca trees which belonged to his share, to Prasanna-Pārśvadēva of the bēṇḍi of Taḷḷingēre known as Brāhmaṇa-Jina-prāsāda. The temple was built by Chāḷukya-Brahma-Jina-Brāhmaṇan of Bhuvanabhuṣaṇa-basti in Bhuvananātha-vishaya, a sub-division of Poṇṇamāravati-sime, north of Dakshiṇa-Madhurā in the southern Pāṇḍya country. From the produce of this garden land āmpūrvavāhana were to be constructed of stone, the basti from its upāna to stupi, the mahā-maṇḍapa, bhadra, Lakshmīmaṇḍapa, gōpura, enclosure (paristāra), lestōna (vandanamāḷē), Mānasthambha and makarattōraṇa.

cells.date: Śaka 1183, Durmati, Chaitra, ba. di. 8 Friday.
cells.remarks: Describes the greatness of the Śaiva teacher Viśvēśvara-Śiva-Deśika, the dīkshā-guru and the rājaguru of the queen's father Gaṇapati. Registers the gift of the village of Mandaram in Veli-nāḍu-vishaya, to the teacher Viśvēśvara-Śambhu together with the village Veia-gaṇḍi. The teacher is stated to have consecrated therein a temple, founded a monastery and a choultry and a matha (matha-Gōlaki) and also allotted land for the maintenance of the temple, to the Suddha-Śaiva monastery to the mater-nity-hospital, and a feeding-house also founded by him.

cells.place: On the same pillar
cells.remarks: Faintly engraved and partly mutilated. Registers the gift of six perpetual lamps to the temple of Viśvanāthadēva at Viśvanāthu-Gōlagiri on the bank of the river Krishṇavēṇī by Rājagurudēvara, i.e., the royal preceptor (Viśēṣavara) Śivāchārya and of 25 cows for each lamp. The artisan (śilpi-āchārya) Guḍḍōja and the smith (akkarasāla) Prōju also received gifts of land. Gifts of land for dancing girls were made by the king and the queen, and the village was given from the Rājaguru. The temples of Sumanathadēva and the mauṇa (kṣētra) Anōju, Naṇṇōju, and Poṇṇōju attached to the Viśvanātha temple also received gifts.

cells.place: On a pillar lying in a doṅka to the south of Peḍa-Parimi.
cells.date: Śaka 1586, Krōdhi, Āshāḍha śu. di. 2, Wednes-day.
cells.remarks: The people of 'Taṇḍikoṇḍa (the mokhasa village of Saidu Abdulla) altogether three of them) came and represented the dispute that the people of (the) village of Taṇḍikoṇḍa and a particular land (in dispute) belonged to Taṇḍikoṇḍa and that the Parimi people were causing unnecessary riot for its possession. The dispute was heard and decided in favour of the former and new boundary stones were ordered to be put up in places not accessible to people.

cells.location: Penumuka
cells.place: On a broken pillar lying in front of the Gōkarpēśvara temple
cells.remarks: States that Proya-Lankagaru employed at the gate of the royal palace remitted for the merit of the king, all unlawful collections like kaṅka and gaḍḍayadaṇḍa on temple vrittis and puṭṭi-koluvu, puṭṭi-koluvu, upukriti, sonkamu, paula-pillari and kānika on the vrittis of the mahājanas, in the villages (named) of his nāyakatvam, and put up this dāna-śāsana before the Gauriśvara-Mahādēva temple of Ponumbuluva. Mentions the mahājanas of Draṭi-gallu. On the third face of the pillar are given sketches of the two standard cubit measures used in measuring lands.

cells.remarks: States that Vālayanti wife of a certain Churya (or Juriya) Ammaṇa-Prēggada built the temple of Vallabhēśvara or Ammiya-Ammam-Vallabhēśvara at Jonnalagadda, and gave 3 kha of land to Sūnyābharaṇa-Paṇḍita the priest of the temple, for lamps to the god. She also gave 1 kha to the couch-blower and 2 kha and 10 ma of land for perpetual lamps and daily offerings.

cells.place: On a slab set up near the Śiva temple at Maḍipādu (same taluk, same district).
cells.remarks: Mentions a number of Purāṇamahā-puṇyaksHhētras of whom the first was Krishṇāratama ; next came Kāmab'a-dhāsara,ma; then Kāsī, then Rāmagōpāla-dhāma, then Raghūttamāśrama; then Rāmapāla. This teother Rēghuramāsērana-Srīpāda consecrated the temple of Rāmeśvara on the bank of the Krishnā and one of Dakshiṇamūrti under the Pel-tre and put up this sāsana. The good of the varṇāśrama-pilgrims up to this sāsanam is like the merit of a bath in the holy Gangā at this holy spot. It describes the greatness of the place quoting a story from the Skanda-purāṇa that even the holy river Ganges was purified of the heinous sin of having come into contact with a Brāhmaṇa widow that had committed sati by taking a bath at this holy spot where the Kriehnā flows northward.
